record.name: Tennessee Driver Services Multi-Channel AI
record.organisation: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security
record.description: Tennessee's Department of Safety and Homeland Security deployed AI-powered tools across chat (December 2025), email (February 2026), and voice channels to handle public enquiries about driver services. The system uses the agency's website as a single source of truth to answer questions autonomously, handling approximately 1,000 daily chat interactions with a 70% resolution rate and operating 24/7 to bridge the gap between high demand (3,000-5,000 daily contacts) and limited staff capacity (1,000).
record.novelty: Using the public website as the sole data source creates a feedback loop where AI errors reveal website inaccuracies, enabling rapid iterative content correction. The system can be reconfigured within minutes to address emerging situations like weather-related closures or scam alerts without traditional technical deployment delays.
record.stakeholders: Tennessee citizens seeking driver services information, TDOS customer service staff who handle the 20% of escalated queries, and TDOS management benefiting from 24/7 automated coverage.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously answers 70% of queries, deflects 10% of non-genuine messages, and escalates 20% to humans without requiring human initiation per interaction. When configured with new use cases—such as identifying scam text enquiries or providing county-specific closure status during an ice storm—it autonomously handles these scenarios 'within minutes of the need being identified,' whereas previously a human agent would have needed to look up that information.
record.tech_details: Built on Zendesk's agentic AI platform with a retrieval architecture drawing exclusively from the agency's public website as the single source of truth. Deployed across three channels—chat (live), email (live), and voice (in final testing)—with text-back capabilities for voice to share links post-call.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Tennessee: AI-powered customer service across chat, email, and voice

record.name: JnA AI Bot
record.description: A WhatsApp-based AI assistant that automatically scans community health data from the Jamii ni Afya platform at month-end, identifies priority trends such as rising disease cases, and generates ready-to-use supervision agendas with talking points and anticipated questions for community health worker meetings. Piloted across two districts in Zanzibar with supervisors and community health workers.
record.novelty: Brings automated data synthesis and agenda generation directly into supervisors' existing WhatsApp workflows rather than requiring new apps or dashboards; co-designed with frontline supervisors to ensure insights support collaborative problem-solving rather than performance review.
record.stakeholders: Community health supervisors, community health workers (CHWs), Ministry of Health, D-tree, Dalberg Data Insights, Dalberg Design; ultimately households receiving targeted health education.
record.agentic_rationale: The bot autonomously scans recent data in a supervisor's catchment area near month-end, selects priority topics to flag (e.g., 'Rising child fever cases'), generates complete coaching agendas including learning objectives and talking points, and responds to follow-up questions in plain language without human initiation of each step.
record.tech_details: WhatsApp-based interface; uses JnA platform data; generates trend briefs and conversational responses grounded in Ministry of Health guidance; designed to operate on community-level aggregated data with guardrails excluding individual patient records and clinical diagnoses.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Zanzibar: Jamii ni Afya AI bot

record.name: CHA AI Assistant
record.description: A WhatsApp-based AI tool that translates raw data from Kenya's Electronic Community Health Information System (eCHIS) into timely performance nudges and emerging health trend alerts for Community Health Assistants (CHAs). The assistant automates the synthesis of routine community health data to help CHAs prepare for supervision meetings, identify priorities, and coach Community Health Promoters more effectively.
record.novelty: The tool operates within existing CHA workflows via WhatsApp rather than requiring a new app, and it closes the loop by returning aggregated data insights back to frontline supervisors rather than only flowing upward to national reporting systems.
record.stakeholders: Community Health Assistants (supervisors), Community Health Promoters (frontline workers), Ministry of Health, Amref Health Africa, Dalberg Data Insights, and Dalberg Design.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI assistant autonomously analyzes raw eCHIS data to "summarize patterns, surface trends, and highlight potential issues" without CHAs manually reviewing each CHP's data, delivering "timely performance nudges and emerging health trend alerts" at month-end to identify priorities for upcoming meetings. CHAs previously had to manually check each CHP's data as it came in; the system now proactively generates insights that 88% of CHAs received and 83% used to guide meetings.
record.tech_details: WhatsApp-based interface; processes aggregated data from Kenya's Electronic Community Health Information System (eCHIS); designed to mirror existing CHA workflow rhythms with end-of-month trend alerts.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Kenya: AI supervision assistant for community health

record.name: Automated Aviation Safety Issue Analysis App
record.organisation: Aviation Safety Technology Institute (Republic of Korea), with National Information Society Agency
record.description: An AI-powered application that automates the processing and analysis of aviation safety data. Users input accident-related documents, and the system automatically translates, summarizes, classifies the accident type, and provides associated risk factors. The app also generates Excel files for secondary analysis and retrieves similar historical accident cases. It was developed to address inefficiencies in manual data processing by specialized analysts and support compliance with ICAO international standards for national aviation safety management.
record.novelty: The system represents a shift from manual data integration and analysis by specialized analysts to automated, end-to-end processing of unstructured aviation accident documents using generative AI. It combines document ingestion, multilingual translation, summarization, classification, and risk factor extraction in a single automated workflow.
record.stakeholders: Safety managers and data analysts at airlines, airports, national aviation agencies, and the Aviation Safety Technology Institute; ultimately the flying public who benefit from improved safety.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously executes a multi-step analytical workflow upon document input: it 'automatically classifies the accident type' and 'provides associated risk factors' without human initiation of each step. The source states that inputting documents 'triggers translation and summarization' and that the app was developed to validate 'automation performance' for 'AI-based aviation safety data processing, safety issue identification, and document generation'.
record.tech_details: Built using a large language model (LLM) fine-tuned on Q&A datasets derived from SKYbrary aviation accident articles, with an established aviation accident classification system and risk factor database. The system preprocesses data into LLM-understandable format and was optimized through continuous technical review.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Automated Analysis of Aviation Safety Issues: Hyper-Scale AI PoC

record.name: Fire Access Route and Evacuation Route Guidance System
record.organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
record.description: An AI and IoT-integrated system that analyzes real-time building data to calculate optimal evacuation routes for occupants and access routes for firefighters during fire incidents. It extends beyond traditional alarm notifications to provide dynamic, data-driven guidance for emergency response. Launched in 2024.
record.novelty: Moves beyond static alarm systems to real-time, adaptive route optimization that simultaneously serves both evacuees and emergency responders using live sensor data.
record.stakeholders: Building occupants, firefighters, fire safety managers, and the National Information Society Agency as implementing body.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously analyzes real-time information and provides optimal routes without requiring human initiation of each calculation; it independently determines and delivers evacuation and access strategies based on live data analysis during active fire incidents.
record.tech_details: Integrates AI with IoT sensors for real-time data collection and processing; specific models or platforms not stated.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Development of a Fire Access Route and Evacuation Route Guidance System based on the BDApp (Fire Remote Control Service)

record.name: AI Prediction and Control Solution for Fine Dust Reduction
record.description: An AI and IoT-enabled system deployed in multi-use public facilities (subway stations, airports, shopping malls, hospitals) that predicts real-time changes in fine dust concentrations and automatically regulates indoor air quality. It replaces traditional periodic filter replacement and manual ventilation adjustments with automated detection and optimal air quality maintenance measures to protect user health.
record.novelty: Moves beyond reactive, manual facility management to predictive, autonomous control of indoor air quality by integrating AI prediction with IoT sensor networks for real-time environmental regulation.
record.stakeholders: Users of multi-use public facilities, facility management operators, and the National Information Society Agency.
record.agentic_rationale: The system detects fine dust concentrations in real time and automatically executes optimal air quality maintenance measures without requiring human initiation for each ventilation adjustment or control action.
record.tech_details: Combines AI prediction models with IoT sensor networks for real-time fine dust monitoring and automated control of ventilation and air filtration systems.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Development of AI Prediction and Control Solution for Fine Dust Reduction in Multi-Use

record.name: Yukti
record.description: Yukti is a bilingual voice AI mentor designed to help engineering students build AI and machine learning projects for their portfolios. Operating in Tamil and English through a Telegram bot, it conducts Socratic mentoring conversations via voice calls to guide students through problem-solving rather than providing direct answers. The pilot currently serves over 1,100 students in Tamil Nadu's state skills programme.
record.novelty: The system employs a Socratic questioning approach where the AI asks follow-up questions rather than giving answers, designed specifically to prevent students from bypassing learning. It features proactive outreach capabilities, autonomously contacting disengaged students to understand barriers, and operates bilingually to bridge language gaps in technical education.
record.stakeholders: Engineering students across Tamil Nadu, particularly those outside metropolitan centres with limited mentorship access; Tamil Nadu Skill Development Corporation; Sustainable Living Lab India (implementer).
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously reaches out to students who had not been engaging to understand barriers they face, and conducts mentoring conversations using Socratic dialogue—asking follow-up questions and guiding students toward working through problems themselves without a human initiating each exchange. After conversations, it autonomously shares action items with students.
record.tech_details: Speech-to-speech architecture using Google Gemini as the underlying model, with an added context layer specific to course content and mentorship processes. Deployed as a Telegram bot that initiates voice callbacks to students' phones and supports multiple personas for different mentoring stages (e.g., presentation coaching, technical questions).

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Yukti: Conversational AI voice agent mentorship platform

record.name: Youth Policy Customized Platform
record.organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
record.description: The platform automatically aggregates and categorizes fragmented youth policy data from central ministries, local governments and public institutions nationwide. It uses AI to deliver personalized policy recommendations to young people and enables direct in-platform applications via Direct Link Policy (DLP) technology, complemented by real-time notifications for key benefits.
record.novelty: It consolidates previously siloed government policy information into a unified, proactive service that automates the entire journey from discovery to application, mirroring the user experience of popular private-sector platforms.
record.stakeholders: Young citizens seeking benefits, parents and caregivers (including those in Seoul’s Borderline Intelligence Program), and public officials using accumulated data to identify children requiring targeted educational support.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously executes multi-step workflows: it automatically collects and categorizes nationwide policy data without manual curation, determines eligibility and recommends personalized policies via AI, and initiates applications through DLP (Direct Link Policy) technology while dispatching real-time notifications, constituting an "automated application system" that does not require human initiation for each step.
record.tech_details: Employs AI for personalized recommendations, DLP (Direct Link Policy) technology for integrated application submission, and continuous data learning to improve accuracy; aggregates data from central and local government sources through interfaces modeled on private platforms popular with youth.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: AI-Based Customized Youth Policy Recommendations and Notifications

record.name: Legi-Assist
record.description: An open-source tool that automatically ingests and analyzes new Maryland state legislation nightly using large language models. It converts bill PDFs to machine-readable text, programmatically detects and excludes struck-through (repealed) text to analyze only current law, compares bill content against agency profiles to determine relevance, and delivers personalized, ranked shortlists of relevant bills to over 120 state agencies each morning.
record.novelty: Purpose-built capability to interpret legal formatting (strikethrough text denoting repealed law) that general AI tools typically misread as active text, combined with a relevance engine that matches bills against detailed agency profiles to surface substantive connections missed by keyword searches.
record.stakeholders: Over 120 Maryland state agencies and teams receiving daily tailored bill rankings, legislative staff, the Innovation Team's data scientists, and other state governments adopting the open-source code.
record.agentic_rationale: The system runs autonomously overnight during legislative sessions to pull new bills from the General Assembly feed, process PDFs, analyze content using LLMs against agency profiles to determine relevance and affected parties, and generate/distribute ranked shortlists to over 120 agencies without a human initiating analysis for each individual bill. It concretely decides which bills affect which agencies and explains the relevance reasoning.
record.tech_details: Built internally using large language models for natural language processing and relevance matching, with custom programming to detect strikethrough formatting in legislative PDFs. The system integrates with the Maryland General Assembly's bill feed and maintains a database of agency profiles for the relevance engine.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Legi-Assist: How Maryland built an open-source tool to track and analyse legislation using AI

record.name: AI-powered Initial Counseling for Welfare Blind Spots
record.organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
record.description: An AI system that analyzes big data on utility disconnections and welfare crisis app reports to proactively identify at-risk households, then initiates automated phone calls to assess welfare needs across health, economic, employment, housing and safety domains. The service transmits consultation results to local government officials who provide in-depth counseling and support. Launched nationwide across 229 local governments in November 2024 after pilots, it served 220,000 people in 2024 with plans to reach 500,000 annually.
record.novelty: Proactively identifies welfare blind spots through real-time big data surveillance of utility disconnections combined with autonomous AI outreach, replacing passive application-based systems with predictive intervention.
record.stakeholders: Vulnerable households facing utility disconnections, local government welfare departments, and the National Information Society Agency.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI autonomously initiates initial consultation calls to individuals identified via big data analysis and, during the conversation, assesses 'the nature of the crisis and welfare needs—such as health, economic, employment, housing, and safety' before transmitting results to officials without human initiation of each contact.
record.tech_details: Utilizes big data analysis of utility disconnection records (electricity, water, gas), AI-powered voice consultation technology, SMS notification gateways, and integration with the welfare crisis alert app and local government case management systems.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Eliminating Welfare Blind Spots through AI-Powered Initial Counseling

record.name: Shucle AI-powered on-demand transport
record.description: A pilot project in Gödöllő, Hungary testing Shucle, an AI-powered demand-responsive transport platform developed by Hyundai Motor Company. Two vehicles replaced fixed-route buses for 11 weeks, dynamically calculating optimal pickup and dropoff routes in real time based on passenger requests. Wait times fell from 60 to 6 minutes with 2,950 residents using the service.
record.novelty: First deployment of Hyundai's Shucle platform outside South Korea, representing a shift from fixed-schedule public transport to fully dynamic, AI-routed on-demand service in a small European city.
record.stakeholders: Residents of Gödöllő needing public transport, municipality transport planners, local bus operators, Hyundai Motor Company, and the Korean-Hungarian Economic Innovation Partnership Program.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI "calculates the most efficient route to pick up and drop off multiple passengers, adjusting continuously as new requests come in" and "only dispatches vehicles in response to actual ride requests" without human intervention for each routing decision. Vehicles autonomously determine where to go based on real-time demand rather than following predetermined routes or schedules.
record.tech_details: Hyundai's Shucle platform using AI algorithms for real-time route optimization; passenger-facing mobile app for ride requests; integration with existing municipal bus network infrastructure.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Shucle: AI-powered on-demand public transport tested in Hungary

record.name: Diia.AI
record.description: Diia.AI is an AI assistant integrated into Ukraine's Diia platform that allows citizens to complete government services through natural language chat conversations. Rather than navigating portals and forms, users describe their needs in plain language, and the assistant connects to live government databases to retrieve information and complete transactions such as income certificates entirely within the chat. The system aims to reduce administrative burden, with projected savings of over one million citizen-hours annually and a 30% reduction in staff-handled enquiries.
record.novelty: Recognized by the World Record Book as the world's first national AI assistant for government services, it employs a privacy-by-design architecture where all identifying information is replaced with neutral placeholders before reaching the AI model, ensuring sensitive personal data never leaves government-controlled infrastructure while still leveraging commercial language models.
record.stakeholders: Citizens accessing government services (particularly older or less digitally confident users), Ministry of Digital Transformation staff, technology partners Google and KitSoft, and ElevenLabs for voice capabilities.
record.agentic_rationale: The assistant connects to relevant government databases, retrieves the citizen's information, and completes the process within the conversation without requiring users to locate or fill forms manually. Unlike conventional chatbots, it "can complete transactions on the citizen's behalf," such as generating income certificates by autonomously executing the service workflow from natural language requests.
record.tech_details: Built on Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash combined with Ukraine's secure government systems and Diia.Engine national digital infrastructure. Uses a four-stage anonymization process where identifying data is swapped for placeholders before AI processing, with responses matched back to citizens via a secure government layer.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Diia.AI: Ukraine's national AI assistant for government services

record.name: GENAI
record.description: Japan's Digital Agency built GENAI, an in-house generative AI platform running in a closed government environment to help civil servants with administrative tasks including drafting answers to parliamentary questions. It connects to the Government Cloud and uses retrieval-augmented generation on official datasets to ensure accuracy, offering over 30 applications for drafting, summarising, translation and document search. Following a pilot start in May 2025, it entered large-scale pilot in May 2026 reaching 100,000 employees with plans for government-wide launch in FY2027.
record.novelty: Unlike commercial procurements, the platform was developed in-house to handle confidential information in a secure closed environment, and part of its codebase was released as open-source software for reuse by local governments and private firms. It specifically targets the redesign of administrative processes around AI rather than simply adding chat-style tools, with a flagship application that autonomously prepares parliamentary answers by analysing questions, retrieving precedents, and checking for contradictions.
record.stakeholders: Civil servants across Japan's 39 national agencies use the platform to reduce overtime; Diet members receive faster, consistent answers; local governments and private firms can adopt the open-source codebase.
record.agentic_rationale: The flagship application for parliamentary questions 'analyses the submitted questions, searches past answers and supporting documents, drafts a reply consistent with the government's earlier positions, anticipates likely follow-up questions and checks the draft for contradictions', executing a multi-step retrieval and drafting workflow without requiring human initiation of each individual step.
record.tech_details: The platform runs on the Government Cloud in a closed environment with single sign-on access, using retrieval-augmented generation to ground outputs in current legislation and official notices. It integrates multiple models including foreign systems through an OpenAI collaboration and domestically developed Japanese LLMs, selected via a public call for trial use.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: GENAI: Japan's government-built AI platform for its civil service, from drafting parliamentary answers to everyday paperwork

record.name: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
record.description: Singapore's IMDA published the first government framework specifically designed for AI systems that can act autonomously. The framework, launched at Davos in January 2026 and updated to Version 1.5 in May 2026, provides governance guidance across four areas: risk assessment before deployment, accountability mechanisms, technical safeguards, and user transparency. It was developed with input from over 60 organisations including government agencies and major technology providers.
record.novelty: This is the first government-published governance framework anywhere specifically targeting agentic AI rather than generative AI or traditional AI systems. It explicitly addresses risks unique to autonomous action-taking, including irreversible actions, cross-system error propagation, and emergent behaviors from multi-agent interactions.
record.stakeholders: Government agencies deploying agentic AI, private sector organisations building or procuring agents, citizens interacting with public services, and technology providers including AWS, Google, DBS, and Salesforce.
record.agentic_rationale: The framework defines agentic AI as systems that "can plan a series of steps, draw on databases and other tools, and carry out actions without a person signing off on each one," with concrete examples including amending citizen records, authorising payments, issuing notifications, and passing tasks to other agents to complete longer workflows. It specifically addresses risks where "the action may already be done by the time anyone notices."
record.tech_details: The framework references the Government Technology Agency's Agentic Risk and Capability Framework for sample controls, connects to AI Verify Foundation's testing tools, and aligns with data-protection and financial regulator guidance. IMDA is preparing separate testing guidance extending earlier LLM testing kits.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Singapore's governance framework for agentic AI: The first guide for AI systems that act on their own

record.name: Puerto Rico AI-powered Hiring Platform
record.description: A standardized digital hiring platform launched in 2024 to unify recruitment across Puerto Rico's government agencies, replacing fragmented paper-based processes. It uses machine learning and natural-language processing to parse resumes, identify candidate skills, and match them to vacancy requirements while masking names to reduce bias.
record.novelty: It consolidates 56 separate agency-specific hiring systems into one platform that automatically screens and matches candidates by skills rather than keywords, and proactively suggests additional matching vacancies to applicants to broaden the talent pool.
record.stakeholders: Job candidates seeking government employment, HR staff at nine participating Puerto Rican government agencies including the Department of Education, and the Financial Oversight and Management Board.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI autonomously handles the initial screening to shortlist candidates by skills without human intervention for each application, reading resumes and identifying skills to match against vacancy requirements. It also proactively shows applicants other open positions across government that fit their skills, stating that 'the AI handles the initial screening to shortlist candidates by skills' and 'shows the applicant other open positions across government that fit their skills'.
record.tech_details: Built on Eightfold AI's talent intelligence platform, utilizing machine learning and natural-language processing to analyse unstructured text in resumes and applications for skills extraction and matching.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Puerto Rico's AI-powered hiring platform: Matching candidates to government jobs by skills

record.name: Multi-agent AI system for ALLEGRO IT change requests
record.description: A multi-agent AI system that automatically converts free-text IT change requests for the ALLEGRO social benefits system into structured Jira tasks. Processing approximately 1,000 requests monthly, the system saves an estimated 100 to 130 staff hours per month by extracting key information, structuring steps, and drafting task entries with titles, descriptions, categories, and priorities.
record.novelty: The system employs four distinct AI agents coordinated via CrewAI to handle sequential stages of document processing, from information extraction to Jira entry drafting and error checking. It runs entirely on the agency's sovereign infrastructure using open-source or privacy-compliant models (Aleph Alpha, LLaMA, Mistral), demonstrating that multi-agent AI can operate within strict government data protection constraints without external cloud dependencies.
record.stakeholders: Federal Employment Agency IT staff (40,000 ALLEGRO users), domain experts who review AI outputs, and Capgemini as the technology implementation partner.
record.agentic_rationale: Four agents execute a sequential workflow without human intervention at each step: the first reads documents to identify problems, affected systems, and required actions; the second organizes this into structured steps; the third drafts complete Jira entries with titles, descriptions, categories, and priorities; and a fourth (in development) checks drafts for errors, inconsistencies, and duplicates before human review.
record.tech_details: The system uses CrewAI, an open-source multi-agent orchestration platform, to coordinate models including Aleph Alpha, LLaMA, and Mistral hosted entirely on the BA's internal infrastructure. It incorporates document chunking processes to handle long documents exceeding model context limits.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Germany: AI agents that turn IT change requests into structured tasks

record.name: TAMM (AutoGov)
record.organisation: Department of Government Enablement (DGE), Abu Dhabi
record.description: TAMM is Abu Dhabi's unified digital platform aggregating services from over 30 government entities into a single app and website. TAMM 4.0 features an AI assistant that completes transactions on users' behalf and AutoGov, described as the world's first transactional AI public servant, which automatically handles recurring tasks such as license renewals, utility payments, and healthcare bookings without requiring individual requests once user preferences are set.
record.novelty: AutoGov represents a shift from passive assistance to proactive execution, acting as a 'transactional AI public servant' that performs recurring government tasks automatically without being prompted each time. The platform integrates more than 30 disparate government bodies into a single interface with autonomous service completion capabilities.
record.stakeholders: Abu Dhabi residents (citizens and expatriates), over 30 government entities including police, health, municipal and transport bodies, the Department of Government Enablement, and technology partners Microsoft and G42.
record.agentic_rationale: AutoGov is designed to handle recurring tasks such as renewing licences, making utility payments, and booking routine healthcare appointments automatically. Once a user sets their preferences, those actions can be carried out without being requested each time. The assistant also completes many services on the customer's behalf rather than only guiding them to a form.
record.tech_details: Built on large language models provided by Microsoft and G42, with G42 supplying a sovereign Arabic-language model and contributing to local cloud infrastructure. The platform supports more than 90 languages and operates within defined government standards and limits.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: TAMM: Abu Dhabi's AI assistant for completing government services through a single app

record.name: Bellwether (Project Ground Truth)
record.description: The City of Kansas City partnered with X, The Moonshot Factory to automate FEMA preliminary damage assessments after natural disasters. The Bellwether system deploys drones to capture high-resolution aerial imagery and uses AI to automatically classify property damage according to FEMA standards (destroyed, major, minor, affected, intact). In a simulated disaster exercise covering 169 acres, the system completed damage assessments in 20 minutes with 96% accuracy, compared to an estimated 78 man-hours for manual methods.
record.novelty: First city to automate FEMA preliminary damage assessments using AI as a 'Phase Zero' first responder that can operate while ground conditions remain hazardous. Replaces subjective human ground surveys with deterministic machine classification of drone imagery.
record.stakeholders: City of Kansas City emergency management staff and volunteers, FEMA, and residents affected by natural disasters who require rapid access to state and federal aid.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously executes the complete assessment workflow: drones fly pre-programmed paths to capture imagery, the Bellwether engine stitches images into a geomosaic and segments it into individual parcels, and an AI model assesses each structure to assign FEMA damage classification scores (e.g., destroyed, major, minor) without human intervention for each individual property evaluation.
record.tech_details: Drone-captured high-resolution aerial imagery processed through a geomosaic stitching pipeline, with the Bellwether engine performing image segmentation and AI-based structural assessment against FEMA classification standards.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Project Ground Truth: Using drones and AI to automatically measure post-disaster damage

record.name: Octopus Triage System
record.description: An AI-powered intake and prioritization platform that automates municipal project triage by analyzing submissions, routing them to appropriate technical teams, and objectively scoring them against municipal value pillars. It replaces manual, subjective prioritization methods with a data-driven framework to ensure resources are allocated to high-impact initiatives.
record.novelty: Integrates generative AI with the Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF) agile prioritization model to objectively score projects against Council Priorities and financial criteria, eliminating 'loudest voice' resource allocation. It generates early complexity and cost estimates automatically to guide municipal resource planning.
record.stakeholders: Municipal technical teams receiving routed projects, internal project proponents, city council setting strategic priorities, and municipal administration managing resource allocation.
record.agentic_rationale: The system uses the Gemini API to automatically analyze and route project descriptions to the correct technical teams without human triage. It autonomously scores and prioritizes submissions using the WSJF model against municipal value pillars, directing resources to high-value work without requiring human initiation of each routing or prioritization decision.
record.tech_details: Built on the Gemini API for content analysis and classification, implements a Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF) scoring algorithm, and developed using open-source tools within the City's existing technical infrastructure.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Octopus Triage System: An AI-powered intake and prioritization solution

record.name: AL21
record.description: AL21 is an AI-powered universal access layer that enables citizens to browse the web and complete municipal procedures using natural language through cyberkiosks and Smart Centres. The system centralises municipal services into a single multilingual access point designed to bridge the digital divide for elderly and disabled users. It currently resolves approximately 500 administrative procedures and over 1,000 citizen queries daily, reducing document issuance times from one month to two days.
record.novelty: The project integrates a tripartite AI architecture—comprising intention classification, conversational Q&A, and ethical moderation—to automate end-to-end administrative processing via RPA rather than merely providing information. Its hybrid municipal-cloud infrastructure and hardware cyberkiosks create a fully inclusive, zero-cost access channel for disadvantaged groups.
record.stakeholders: Primary beneficiaries are citizens facing the digital divide, particularly the elderly and people with disabilities; implementing partners include the Valencian Innovation Agency (AVI), the ELLIS Alicante Foundation, the Digital Intelligence Centre (CENID), and a local Alicante start-up as the technical provider.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously executes administrative formalities through its 'Intention Classification Module' which triggers Robotic Process Automation (RPA) to resolve procedures—processing 500 procedures daily without human initiation of each step—and operates 'conversational analysis and summary broadcasting robots' for automated information dissemination.
record.tech_details: The architecture comprises three parallel AI modules: an Intention Classification Module (with RPA), a Query&Answer module based on web scraping, and a moderation module for ethical biases. It uses a hybrid infrastructure combining on-premise municipal data processing centres (DPC) for base information with cloud resources for AI logic, trained on over 100,000 citizen calls.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Bridging the Digital Divide

record.name: Smart Station Project
record.description: Seoul Metro's Smart Station Project integrates IoT sensors, computer vision AI, deep learning, and 3D digital twin technology to automate facility management, safety monitoring, and emergency response across subway stations. The system enables real-time detection of abnormalities, automatic facility control, and proactive alerts to staff, reducing response time to safety accidents by 75% and improving operation rates by 65%.
record.novelty: First system of its kind in Korea to combine 3D digital twin visualization with AI-powered autonomous detection and response capabilities for subway operations, creating a standardized IoT platform that integrates previously siloed legacy systems across multiple lines.
record.stakeholders: Seoul Metro staff, daily passengers (7 million+), mobility-impaired users, Samsung SDS and technology partners, national safety agencies including National Crisis Management Center and National Police Agency.
record.agentic_rationale: The deep learning engine 'automatically detect[s] all abnormalities and deploy[s] immediate responses by sending real-time alarms 24 hours a day' without human initiation; facilities 'are operated automatically according to the predetermined rules' when pre-defined abnormal situations occur; and the system 'initiates immediate responses' to COVID-19 safety violations and fare evasions detected through computer vision, enabling staff to 'make decisions immediately and dispatch personnel as needed thanks to AI recognizing issues and sending proactive alerts'.
record.tech_details: Samsung SDS Brightics IoT platform, deep learning AI imaging analysis, computer vision AI, 3D digital twin systems, standardized IoT platform with protocol lake for heterogeneous device integration, mobile app integration for real-time passenger information.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Smart Station for Future Urban Train

record.name: ClearVision Risk-Based Inspection System
record.organisation: Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing (MoMRAH), Saudi Arabia
record.description: An AI-powered inspection platform that uses machine learning to cluster cases, prioritize incidents, and dispatch inspectors based on risk rather than static first-in-first-out rules. The system was developed by MoMRAH's Digital Transformation and Smart Cities Deputyship through the 'ClearVision' team to address visual pollution and expanded to retail, health, excavation and other inspection types. It processes over 3 million annual cases through the Baladi mobile platform.
record.novelty: Replaced static inspection scheduling with dynamic, learning-based dispatch that identifies 1,200+ focused risk areas and clusters cases to save 25-30% of inspector visits. Created new organizational structures including dedicated departments for model ideation, hosting/operations, and smart operations.
record.stakeholders: Municipal inspectors, government officials as business owners, private sector technology providers, citizens reporting via Baladi platform, and municipalities as operational implementers.
record.agentic_rationale: The Risk Based Dispatching engine autonomously identifies priority areas and directs inspector deployment without fixed static rules, using feedback loops from historical cases and actual visits to dynamically learn and adjust. The system proactively determines 'location-near and similar cases' and 'focused areas' for inspection rather than following human-initiated sequential scheduling.
record.tech_details: Three integrated AI engines: Case Clustering (grouping similar nearby incidents), Case Prioritization (identifying top quartile requiring imminent response), and Risk Based Dispatching (dynamic inspector allocation). Built using agile methodology with external parties for model QC and verification. Expanded to 14+ engines with two master engines for cross-classification.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Analytics and AI Solutions for Risk Based Inspections

record.name: Tengai recruitment robot
record.description: The Municipality of Upplands-Bro deployed the Tengai robot in June 2019 to conduct recruitment interviews with the aim of reducing bias in hiring processes. The system autonomously screens candidates to create shortlists, conducts behavioral interviews including adaptive follow-up questions, and analyzes responses to assess problem-solving skills and competencies before human recruiters conduct final motivation interviews. Following a one-week pilot, the municipality permanently adopted the system, reporting successful initial results and significant media attention.
record.novelty: Tengai was one of the first interviewer robots deployed in public sector recruitment, designed specifically to mitigate unconscious bias compared to traditional human interviews. The system combines automated candidate screening with autonomous, adaptive interviewing capabilities that analyze candidate behaviors in real-time.
record.stakeholders: Municipality recruitment and staffing agency staff, job candidates applying for municipal positions, and Furhat Robotics as the AI consultancy partner.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously "identify candidates with the highest general performance score" to create shortlists, "conducts the interviews to assess the candidates by analysing their behaviours, problem-solving capacities and other skills," and "If needed, the robot is able to ask follow-up questions" before analyzing and combining interviews with competency scores, all without requiring human initiation of each specific step.
record.tech_details: Tengai is a physical interviewer robot developed through collaboration between the municipality and Furhat Robotics, utilizing AI to analyze candidate behaviors and responses during interviews.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Tengai - Robot in recruitment processes
